rĕd-ămo ,
		āre, v. a., 
I.to love back, love in return, return love for love
			(formed by Cic. after the Gr. ἀντιφιλεῖν): qui vel amare vel, ut ita dicam, redamare
			possit, Cic. Lae). 14, 49; 
				“also in late Lat.,”
				 Macr. S. 6, 9, 6
			; Symm. Ep. 3, 2;
				Ambros. in Luc. 5, § 75;
			Leo M. Sern. 72; App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 19,
				18.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
